accepted.s: Doddi Komaraiah was killed at which place on 4 July 1946, triggering the Telangana Armed Struggle?
accepted.x: Doddi Komaraiah was killed by the deshmukh's men at Kadavendi in Jangaon on 4 July 1946, triggering the Telangana Armed Struggle.
accepted.tq: Use the place-and-date combination to distinguish the trigger of the Telangana struggle from later incidents of the Srikakulam struggle.
accepted.sec: Telangana and Srikakulam armed struggles - trigger, period, end, memoirs

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Telangana Armed Struggle:
1. Peasants seized land during the struggle.
2. Village soviets were established in the affected areas.
3. The struggle was directed against Nizam's jagirdars, deshmukhs and the practice of vetti.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The Telangana peasants seized land, established village soviets and resisted jagirdars, deshmukhs and vetti.
accepted.tq: Check each statement against the struggle's land, organisational and anti-feudal features before selecting the combined option.
accepted.sec: Telangana and Srikakulam armed struggles - trigger, period, end, memoirs

accepted.s: The ceasefire that marked the end of the Telangana Armed Struggle in October 1951 followed Soviet advice to the communists to
accepted.x: The ceasefire in October 1951 followed Soviet advice that the communists should work with the Congress.
accepted.tq: Identify the political advice associated with the end of the struggle rather than confusing it with the causes of the movement.
accepted.sec: Telangana and Srikakulam armed struggles - trigger, period, end, memoirs

accepted.s: The immediate trigger of the Srikakulam Girijana struggle was the attack on a tribal meeting near Parvathipuram on
accepted.x: The immediate trigger was the attack on a tribal meeting near Parvathipuram on 31 October 1967, in which two tribals were killed. The incident is also referred to as the Mondemkhal incident.
accepted.tq: Separate the trigger date from the later CPI(ML) announcement and the declaration of the disturbed area.
accepted.sec: Telangana and Srikakulam armed struggles - trigger, period, end, memoirs

accepted.s: Which one of the following was NOT among the groups primarily opposed during the Srikakulam Girijana struggle?
accepted.x: The Srikakulam struggle was directed against traders, moneylenders, landlords and gothi or bonded labour. Nizam's jagirdars were associated with the Telangana Armed Struggle.
accepted.tq: Find the group belonging to the other armed struggle by comparing the opposing social forces.
accepted.sec: Telangana and Srikakulam armed struggles - trigger, period, end, memoirs

accepted.s:
Arrange the following events relating to the Srikakulam struggle in chronological order:
A. The CPI(ML) announced its formation in relation to the movement.
B. A tribal meeting near Parvathipuram was attacked.
C. Panchadhi Krishnamurthy was killed at Jalantra Kota.
D. Srikakulam was declared a disturbed area.
accepted.x: The correct order is the 31 October 1967 tribal meeting attack, the 22 April 1969 CPI(ML) announcement, the 27 May 1969 killing of Panchadhi Krishnamurthy, and the 16 June 1970 declaration of the disturbed area.
accepted.tq: Place the events by their dates first, then eliminate sequences that reverse the 1967 trigger and the 1969 developments.
accepted.sec: Telangana and Srikakulam armed struggles - trigger, period, end, memoirs

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the end of the Srikakulam Girijana struggle?
o: Srikakulam was declared a disturbed area on 16 June 1970, and the movement was crushed by 1971.
It ended with a ceasefire in October 1951 after Soviet advice.
It ended immediately after the Parvathipuram incident in 1967.
It ended when the Andhra Communist Party was formed at Kakinada in 1936.
accepted.x: Srikakulam was declared a disturbed area on 16 June 1970, Vempatapu Satyam and Adibhatla Kailasam were killed at Barikonda on 10 July 1970, and the movement was crushed by 1971.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the end sequence of Srikakulam from the October 1951 end of the Telangana struggle.
accepted.sec: Telangana and Srikakulam armed struggles - trigger, period, end, memoirs

accepted.s: Panchadhi Krishnamurthy, a leader associated with the Srikakulam struggle, was killed at Jalantra Kota on
accepted.x: Panchadhi Krishnamurthy was killed at Jalantra Kota on 27 May 1969. The 10 July 1970 date relates to the killing of Satyam and Kailasam at Barikonda.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the dates of the CPI(ML) announcement, the killing at Jalantra Kota and the later Barikonda encounter.
accepted.sec: Telangana and Srikakulam armed struggles - trigger, period, end, memoirs

accepted.s:
Match the following sessions of the Nizam's Andhra Mahasabha with their presidents:

List-I (Year and venue)
 a. 1935, Siricilla
 b. 1941, Chilkur
 c. 1943, Hyderabad
 d. 1944, Bhuvanagiri

List-II (President)
 i. Ravi Narayana Reddy
 ii. K.V. Ranga Reddy
 iii. Madapati Hanumantha Rao

Select the correct answer using the code below.
accepted.x: Madapati Hanumantha Rao presided at Siricilla in 1935; Ravi Narayana Reddy at Chilkur in 1941; K.V. Ranga Reddy at Hyderabad in 1943; and Ravi Narayana Reddy at Bhuvanagiri in 1944.
accepted.tq: Build the answer from the fixed venue–year pairs and then verify the repeated presidency of Ravi Narayana Reddy.
accepted.sec: Nizam's Andhra Mahasabha - presidents, period, communist takeover

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the significance of the 1944 Bhuvanagiri session of the Nizam's Andhra Mahasabha?
o: It brought the Mahasabha under communist control, after which a rival Nationalist Andhra Mahasabha broke away.
It was presided over by Suravaram Pratap Reddy as the first session.
It ended the Telangana Armed Struggle through a ceasefire.
It marked the first meeting of the Andhra Communist Party at Kakinada.
accepted.x: The 1944 Bhuvanagiri session came under communist control, and a rival Nationalist Andhra Mahasabha subsequently broke away.
accepted.tq: Identify the institutional consequence of a particular session rather than confusing it with the founding or closing events of other organisations.
accepted.sec: Nizam's Andhra Mahasabha - presidents, period, communist takeover

accepted.s: By the 1940s, the Nizam's Andhra Mahasabha had primarily shifted from language and cultural issues to mobilisation against
o: the integration of princely states alone
accepted.x: By the 1940s, the Mahasabha had become effectively a communist front and mobilised peasants against jagirdari, vetti and taxes, contributing to the armed struggle.
accepted.tq: Recognise the change in the organisation's agenda from cultural demands to agrarian and anti-feudal mobilisation.
accepted.sec: Nizam's Andhra Mahasabha - presidents, period, communist takeover

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: P. Sundarayya — CPI and later CPI(M)
accepted.x: Swami Ramananda Tirtha was a leader of the Hyderabad State Congress and led the Join Indian Union movement; he was not a CPI(M) leader. Ravi Narayana Reddy, Baddam Yella Reddy and P. Sundarayya were associated with the communist movement.
accepted.tq: Find the non-communist political affiliation among leaders otherwise associated with the communist movement.

accepted.s: Makhdoom Mohiuddin is best described as a
o: president of the first Nizam's Andhra Mahasabha
leader of the Hyderabad State Congress's Join Indian Union movement
founder of the Andhra Communist Party at Kakinada
poet and communist leader associated with the Comrades Association
accepted.x: Makhdoom Mohiuddin was a poet and communist leader associated with the Comrades Association.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding bans on communist organisations:
1. The Communist Party was banned in Hyderabad State in December 1946.
2. The Communist Party was banned in Andhra, then part of Madras, in September 1949.
3. The Andhra ban was lifted in October 1951.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The Hyderabad State ban began in December 1946, while the Andhra or Madras ban began in September 1949 and was lifted in October 1951.
accepted.tq: Separate the dates and jurisdictions of the Hyderabad State and Andhra-region bans before choosing the combined option.
accepted.sec: Ban on the Communist Party and lifting → years

accepted.s: Which of the following events is correctly matched with its associated action?
o: 1934 — Hyderabad State ban on the Communist Party was lifted
1948 — Prajasakti was founded as the first Andhra Communist unit
1946 — Chief Minister Prakasam arrested communist leaders
accepted.x: Chief Minister Prakasam arrested communist leaders in 1946. Prajasakti was banned in 1948, while the All-India ban had already been lifted in 1942.
accepted.tq: Check the authority and year together, using swapped action-and-date combinations as the trap.
accepted.sec: Ban on the Communist Party and lifting → years

accepted.s: In 1934, communists met secretly in whose garden at Vijayawada and formed a seven-member committee with P. Sundarayya as secretary?
accepted.x: The secret meeting took place in Katragadda Narayana Rao's garden at Vijayawada in 1934, where a seven-member committee was formed with P. Sundarayya as secretary.
accepted.tq: Combine the precise place, organiser and committee detail to identify the correct founding episode.

accepted.s: Amir Haider Khan's Young Workers League contributed to the communist movement in Andhra by
o: leading the Join Indian Union movement
accepted.x: Amir Haider Khan's Young Workers League, formed in 1929, recruited P. Sundarayya and provided an early organisational root of the communist movement in Andhra.
accepted.tq: Link the organisation, year and individual recruited to identify the movement's early roots.

accepted.s: The first communist unit in Telangana was the Hyderabad State Comrades Association, formed in
accepted.x: The Hyderabad State Comrades Association, regarded as Telangana's first communist unit, was formed in 1939. Its members included Makhdoom Mohiuddin, Raj Bahadur Gour and Syed Ibrahim.
accepted.tq: Use the sequence of early communist milestones to distinguish the first Telangana unit from the Andhra party's formation.
accepted.sec: Communist Party in Andhra - founding year, founders, first units

accepted.s: The third Communist conference held at Vijayawada in July 1943 was significant because it was
o: the first open conference, with Chandra Rajeswara Rao as secretary
the conference at which the CPI split occurred
the first secret meeting of communists in Andhra
the meeting at which the Comrades Association was formed
accepted.x: The third Communist conference at Vijayawada in July 1943 was the first open conference, and Chandra Rajeswara Rao served as secretary.
accepted.tq: Use the conference number and its distinctive organisational feature to reject neighbouring conference details.

formation of the Hyderabad State Congress
imposition of the All-India CPI ban
formation of the Hyderabad State Comrades Association

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the 1964 split in the communist movement:
1. The CPI side included Ravi Narayana Reddy and Chandra Rajeswara Rao.
2. The CPI(M) side included P. Sundarayya and Basavapunnaiah.
3. The CPI side was associated with a pro-Soviet position, while the CPI(M) side was associated with a pro-China position.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Ravi Narayana Reddy and Chandra Rajeswara Rao remained with the CPI, while P. Sundarayya and Basavapunnaiah went with the CPI(M); the two sides were identified respectively with pro-Soviet and pro-China positions.
accepted.tq: Match both leaders and ideological alignments before selecting the complete set of correct statements.
accepted.sec: Communist Party in Andhra - founding year, founders, first units
